result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover glyph coverage, fallback behaviour, real-string testing, Turkish casing and licensing well. B gives a clearer decision rule and concrete replacement fonts with a reminder to check their subsets. It is also more open about what it cannot confirm from the font's name or from where it is. A is more precise about Unicode ranges, since it names Latin Extended-B, which B leaves out, but B is more practical and more honest overall. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name the right characters, explain what happens when a glyph is missing, recommend testing with the real product names and give a sensible fallback plan. B is more precise on coverage: it notes that Latin-1 alone misses Ł, Ş, Ğ and the Vietnamese letters, and that ơ/ư need Latin Extended-B. It also gives line-height clipping and uppercase-accent quality their own section, and offers three clear options, including keeping product names out of the display font. A is strong and names candidate replacement fonts, but its coverage ranges are slightly incomplete and its clipping point is brief.
